title: Parking a Goods Vehicle
whatItIs: Over 7.5 tonnes, a goods vehicle must not be parked on a verge, pavement or central land without police permission. Park off-street where you can.

keyFacts.text: Over 7.5 t (trailer included): you MUST NOT park on a verge, pavement or central land without police permission.
Exception: essential loading or unloading, but then the vehicle MUST NOT be left unattended.
Before leaving, you MUST switch off the engine, headlights and fog lights and apply the handbrake.
On a road or lay-by with a limit over 30 mph, all vehicles MUST show parking lights.

visual.caption: More parking rules for lorry drivers

items.title: At night
items.text: Goods vehicles over 2,500 kg laden MUST NOT be left on a road at night without lights.

items.title: Places to avoid
items.text: Within 10 m of a junction, on a bend, near a bus stop or a level crossing.

items.title: Loading and unloading
items.text: Not where yellow kerb markings and signs show restrictions.

items.title: Security
items.text: Remove the key, lock the vehicle and never leave vehicle documents in it.

a.label: Goods vehicle over 7.5 t
points: MUST NOT park on verges or pavements without police permission
Loading there only if essential, never unattended

b.label: Vehicle up to 7.5 t
points: The 7.5 t verge rule does not apply
Should still avoid pavements unless signs permit

onTheTest.question: When may you park an 18-tonne lorry on a grass verge without police permission?
options: Only if essential for loading, and never unattended
Overnight, if you leave the lights on
At weekends, when traffic is light
onTheTest.why: Over 7.5 t you need police permission, unless it is essential for loading or unloading, and then never unattended.

onTheTest.question: You leave your lorry parked on a 30 mph road at night. What must you do?
options: Nothing, as the limit is 30 mph
Leave the hazard warning lights on
onTheTest.why: Only cars and goods vehicles up to 2,500 kg may park without lights on a 30 mph road.

traps: The 7.5 t limit for verges and pavements includes any trailer.
The 30 mph 'no lights at night' exemption is for goods vehicles up to 2,500 kg, not lorries.
Don't park in passing places on single-track roads.

jurisdictionNotes.text: You MUST NOT park on the pavement or double park (limited exceptions).
In London you MUST NOT park on the pavement (limited exceptions).
